newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Gauteng racing industry to list soon.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Gauteng racing industry to list soon.

text.p: The horse racing industry in South Africa's central Gauteng province is aiming for a listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange as soon as possible, the Department of Finance and Economic Affairs said on Tuesday.
The region's operations are being privatised and as part of the process the industry is to come together into a single corporate structure.
"(The industry) will be listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange as soon as practically possible," the department said.
Another key element of the process will be the bringing in of black empowerment groups who will control 22.5 percent of the new firm.
The company will consist of the assets of Totaliser Agency Board, the Horse Racing Authority and the three racing clubs of Newmarket, Turffontein and Gosforth Park.

Aside from black empowerment groups, the Racing Trust will own 30 percent of the firm, strategic investors and management will get 20 percent and an employee share scheme will account for 2.5 percent.
The general public will get access to 15 percent of the company and the racing public will get 10 percent.

The department said it had agreed to look at the possibility of giving the firm an initial exclusive racing licence for a set period, while the company will also be elegible to apply for other forms of gambling licences.
Gauteng is a densely populated and highly industrialised region containing Johannesburg and Pretoria.
